title: The Lamb that was slain (Apocalypse 5)
hook: the Mass joins this heavenly liturgy (CCC 1090)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the door opened in heaven, and holy, holy, holy. Your line was they rest not.

In Handel's Messiah, audiences stand for the Hallelujah chorus, but it isn't the ending. The Hallelujah closes the second part. The whole work ends later, with a slower, larger chorus and then an Amen that goes on and on, voices climbing over each other. Its words, worthy is the Lamb that was slain, come from the fifth chapter of the Apocalypse, where they're sung in heaven, by a choir far bigger than any concert hall could hold.
screen: `NOT THE HALLELUJAH.` → `THE LAST CHORUS OF MESSIAH.` → `WORTHY IS THE LAMB.`

segments.voice: Chapter five begins with a problem. In the right hand of the one on the throne is a scroll, written inside and out, sealed with seven seals. A strong angel calls out: who is worthy to open it? No one in heaven or on earth or under the earth can. John weeps much, he says. Then an elder tells him: weep not; the Lion of the tribe of Juda, the root of David, has won, and can open the scroll. John turns to look for a lion, and sees a Lamb. Standing, yet looking as though it had been slain. Told a lion, he sees a lamb with its wounds still showing. That's the whole book in one image: the power that wins is a love that was killed and is alive. John's Greek word is arnion, which can mean a little lamb. The Lamb takes the scroll, and heaven erupts. The creatures and the elders fall down with harps and bowls of incense, which the text says are the prayers of the saints. Thousands upon thousands of angels sing, in the Douay-Rheims: "The Lamb that was slain is worthy to receive power, and divinity, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and benediction." Then every creature, in heaven, on earth, under the earth and in the sea, joins in. Catholics hear this at Mass. As the host is broken before Communion, the people sing or say the Lamb of God, and the priest holds up the host and says, behold the Lamb of God. The Catechism says the liturgy on earth already shares in this heavenly one.
screen: `A SCROLL NO ONE CAN OPEN.` · `TOLD A LION, JOHN SEES A LAMB.` · `THE PRAYERS OF THE SAINTS.` · `THE LAMB OF GOD AT EVERY MASS.` · then, large: `THE LAMB THAT WAS SLAIN IS WORTHY.`

segments.voice: Picture the throne, the scroll, the Lamb standing with its wounds showing, and every creature everywhere singing, and let your own small voice be one of them. If you pray, say the Agnus Dei slowly, in your own language or the old Latin, Agnus Dei, qui tollis peccata mundi, miserere nobis, three times, a breath for each. If you don't pray, just picture the Lamb, and notice what it means that the winner has wounds.
Arnion, a little lamb. Apocalypse five: the lamb standing with its wounds still showing, worthy to open the scroll no one else could open. Today's word.
Your line: worthy is the lamb. Told a lion, John saw a lamb. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: At every Mass, while the host is broken, the people sing or say the Agnus Dei, Lamb of God, three times, and the priest then shows the host with the words of John the Baptist, Behold the Lamb of God; the Church teaches that the earthly liturgy shares in the heavenly one.

what a scholar hears: arnion, which can mean 'little lamb', the Apocalypse's name for Christ again and again; announced as a lion, he appears as a lamb, 'standing as it were slain'.
recall: the church that left its first love

chat.says: Why do they call Jesus the Lamb of God at Mass? Lambs seem weak.
options: John is told of a lion, but sees a slain Lamb standing: love that wins.
Because he was a shepherd before he started preaching in Galilee.
It's an old nickname for any gentle person, from Jesus's own village.
chat.meaning: In Apocalypse 5, the Lion who can open the scroll turns out to be a Lamb standing as though slain: the power that wins is love.

notes: Editor review (2026-10-01): hook no longer says what 'most people think'; the words of the final chorus were chosen by the librettist Charles Jennens, so 'Handel took them' became 'they come from'; removed 'well over a thousand years' and 'main title'; the Lamb of God is sung or said during the fraction.
Messiah: the Hallelujah chorus ends Part II; the work closes with 'Worthy is the Lamb' and the Amen chorus. Confirm.
Arnion as a diminutive form ('little lamb'), though in Koine it often means simply 'lamb'. Script says 'can mean'. Confirm.
Agnus Dei in the Roman Mass since the late seventh century (Pope Sergius I): 'well over a thousand years'. Confirm.
CCC 1090 / Sacrosanctum Concilium 8: the earthly liturgy as a foretaste and sharing in the heavenly liturgy. Paraphrased.
Apocalypse 5:5 ('Weep not; behold the lion of the tribe of Juda…') paraphrased with Douay spelling 'Juda'.
